reason: The text contains no explicit statement from Yahweh regarding His desires or will. The narrative (Genesis 34) depicts a tragic violation, followed by deception and violent retaliation by Jacob's sons. Jacob himself expresses concern about the negative consequences of their actions, ultimately cursing their anger and violence. The passage does not present evidence of Yahweh wanting the Hebrew people to be well; rather, it shows Jacob distressed about being brought into disrepute and fearing destruction. No divine expression of concern for the Hebrew people's wellbeing appears in this text.
